apocryphal._note: POPULATED. Entries below list every proper personal name found in public-domain English translations of the Gospel of Thomas, Gospel of Philip, Gospel of Mary, and Protevangelium of James (see text_sources for the exact editions), tagged canonical-overlap / palestinian-typical / atypical. See "method" for how names were extracted and counts estimated, and the scratchpad notes file for which live fetches failed.

entries.name: Jesus
entries.note: Speaker attribution ("Jesus said") opens nearly every one of the 114 sayings; counted as one name throughout.

entries.name: Thomas
entries.note: As "Didymos Judas Thomas" in the incipit (reputed author) and addressed by name in saying 13.

entries.name: Simon Peter
entries.note: Sayings 13 and 114.

entries.name: Matthew
entries.note: Saying 13.

entries.name: Mary
entries.note: Sayings 21 and 114; usually read as Mary Magdalene, text does not disambiguate.

entries.name: Salome
entries.note: Saying 61 (dialogue with Jesus at her couch).

entries.name: James
entries.note: Saying 12, "James the righteous" (James the Just, brother of Jesus).

entries.name: Adam
entries.note: Sayings 46 and 85; OT figure, but also named in the canonical genealogy at Luke 3:38.

entries.name: John the Baptist
entries.note: Saying 46 ("from Adam to John the Baptist").

entries.name: Jesus
entries.note: Personal name "Jesus" as distinct from the title "Christ" (titles excluded from this count).

entries.name: Mary
entries.note: Mother of Jesus, named in the "three Marys" passage (mother / sister / Magdalene, all named Mary).

entries.name: Mary Magdalene
entries.note: Named as the Savior's companion, kissed by him "more than the rest of the disciples."

entries.name: Philip
entries.note: "Philip the apostle said, Joseph the carpenter planted a garden..." - the apostle appears once inside the text that bears his name.

entries.name: Joseph
entries.note: "Joseph the carpenter," father figure of Jesus, discussed re: the wood of the cross.

entries.name: Adam
entries.note: Central to the text's creation discourse; OT figure also named in Luke 3:38.

entries.name: Eve
entries.note: Paired with Adam in the creation discourse; not named in the four canonical Gospels (cf. Paul, 2 Cor 11:3), and not a name attested for living women in Tal Ilan's Palestinian corpus - treated as mythic/symbolic here.

entries.name: Abraham
entries.note: Discussed re: circumcision as a "sign"; also named repeatedly in the canonical Gospels (e.g. Matt 1, John 8).

entries.name: Sophia
entries.note: Valentinian Gnostic personification of Wisdom, treated in the text almost as a character; Greek theological/philosophical name, not a Palestinian Jewish personal name.

entries.name: Echamoth / Echmoth
entries.note: Wordplay pair on "Wisdom"/"Wisdom of death" used as quasi-personal names for the lower and upper Sophia; Coptic-Gnostic coinage, not a real attested name.

entries.name: Mary
entries.note: Protagonist, generally identified as Mary Magdalene; the surviving Coptic/Greek fragments are damaged so exact count is uncertain.

entries.name: Levi
entries.note: Levi the tax collector, identified with Matthew at Mark 2:14/Luke 5:27.

entries.name: Jesus
entries.note: The text overwhelmingly calls him "the Savior"/"the Lord"; the personal name "Jesus" is rare to absent in the surviving pages (the opening pages are lost).

entries.name: Joachim
entries.note: Father of Mary; Hebrew name (form of Jehoiachin/Eliakim), well attested in the period though not a canonical-Gospel character.

entries.name: Anna
entries.note: Mother of Mary; Hannah/Anna is a common attested Jewish woman's name of the period.

entries.name: Zacharias
entries.note: Priest, father of John the Baptist; martyred in the temple in this text's expanded legend.

entries.name: John
entries.note: The infant John the Baptist, hidden with Elizabeth from Herod's soldiers.

entries.name: Salome
entries.note: The skeptical midwife who tests Mary's virginity; same name as the canonical disciple/daughter of Herodias, but a distinct character here.

entries.name: James
entries.note: Narrator ("I, James, wrote this history..."), presented as Joseph's son, i.e. James the Just / brother of the Lord.

entries.name: Reuben / Reubel
entries.note: Rebukes Joachim for offering first; Reuben is an attested patriarchal Hebrew name, though less common than the top names in Ilan's lexicon.

entries.name: Simeon
entries.note: Priest chosen by lot after Zacharias's death, told he would not see death until he had seen the Messiah - echoes Luke 2's Simeon; Simon/Simeon is also the single most common male name in the Gospels/Acts corpus.

entries.name: Annas
entries.note: "Annas the scribe," a minor character who reports Zacharias's absence; same name as the high priest Annas of Luke 3:2/John 18/Acts 4.

Gospel of Thomas.translation: Thomas O. Lambdin (Nag Hammadi Library, Coptic NHC II,2)
Gospel of Thomas.date_of_text: 2nd century (c. 100-150 CE; possibly incorporates earlier independent sayings tradition)

Gospel of Philip.translation: Wesley W. Isenberg (Nag Hammadi Library, Coptic NHC II,3)

Gospel of Mary.translation: Nag Hammadi Library / Berlin Codex (BG 8502) translation as hosted by the Gnostic Society Library
Gospel of Mary.date_of_text: 2nd century (c. 150-200 CE; surviving manuscripts are 3rd-5th c. and fragmentary)

Protevangelium of James.translation: Alexander Walker, Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 8, as hosted by New Advent

apocryphal.method: Named persons were identified by reading/recalling the standard public-domain English translations linked in text_sources (Lambdin for Thomas, Isenberg for Philip, the Gnostic Society Library text for Mary, and Walker's Ante-Nicene Fathers translation for the Protevangelium). Live WebFetch access to gnosis.org, wikisource.org, sacred-texts.com, earlychristianwritings.com and en.wikipedia.org was blocked by this session's network egress proxy for every domain attempted, so extraction relies on Claude's trained knowledge of these well-known texts, cross-checked against WebSearch result snippets (which quote short passages) where possible. Mention counts are therefore APPROXIMATE (all flagged approx:true) - order-of-magnitude occurrence counts per name, not a verified concordance tally. Tagging: canonical-overlap = the same-named person/character also appears in the four canonical Gospels (and, by extension, Acts); palestinian-typical = not a canonical character but the name is a common attested Jewish personal name in Tal Ilan's Palestine 330 BCE-200 CE lexicon (e.g. Joachim, Anna/Hannah, Reuben); atypical = names that are Greco-Egyptian/Gnostic theological coinages or mythic figures not attested as ordinary 1st-century Palestinian Jewish personal names and not named in the canonical Gospels (e.g. Eve, Sophia, Echamoth/Echmoth in Philip). Titles (God, Father, Holy Spirit, Christ, Lord, Savior, Caesar) are excluded even where they stand in for a name.
